node-1.label: A 5-day-old male neonate presented with widespread jaundice

node-2.label: The neonate was a 5-day-old male born at term via vaginal delivery, weighing approximately 2100 g; mother had history of six pregnancies and six live births and was generally healthy except for mild photosensitivity; no history of clay-colored stools, fever, or drug administration

node-3.label: On admission, physical examination showed pale conjunctiva, yellowing of the sclera, generalized jaundice, a few red lesions around the eyes, and mild enlargement of the spleen; pulse was irregular with heart rate about 75 beats per minute; electrocardiogram indicated third-degree atrioventricular block; echocardiography revealed patent foramen ovale without other abnormalities

node-4.label: Blood tests showed hemoglobin 9 g/dL and platelet count 80,000/mm3; blood smear indicated erythrocyte hypochromia, anisocytosis, and poikilocytosis; reticulocyte index, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate were within normal ranges; liver function tests were elevated: AST 760 U/L, ALT 187 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 2045 U/L, total bilirubin 12.4 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 6.2 mg/dL; prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time were normal; TORCH titers, viral hepatitis markers, thyroid function tests, blood and urine cultures for mother and neonate, and tests for galactosemia, tyrosinemia, and phenylketonuria were negative

node-5.label: Abdominal ultrasound showed a normal-sized liver and gall bladder, no bile duct dilation, and no biliary sludge; spleen was mildly enlarged with normal echo pattern; hepatobiliary scintigraphy indicated decreased hepatic uptake with no passage through the intrahepatic bile ducts; initially skin lesions were a few non-scarring red annular plaques around the eyes, and over the next few days they spread to the nasal bridge and upper cheeks, developing sharp and slightly hyperkeratotic borders

attrs.why: New expert laboratory analysis adds ANA 1:640 and anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB >4 index, which are highly specific for neonatal lupus erythematosus and align with the existing AV block, annular periorbital rash, splenomegaly, cytopenias, hepatitis, and maternal photosensitivity. The expert also confirms negative TORCH, viral markers, and cultures. These findings substantially strengthen the diagnosis, increasing confidence from 0.75 to 0.95.

New positive ANA 1:640 and anti-Ro/SSA/anti-La/SSB >4 index strongly favor autoimmune neonatal lupus rather than congenital infection, in addition to the already negative TORCH, viral markers, and cultures reported by the laboratory expert. Confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.05.
node-3 pallor/jaundice/splenomegaly; node-4 anemia/smear support hemolysis; normal retic index, high direct bilirubin, AV block/rash argue against.
node-4 hyperbilirubinemia/elevated enzymes and node-5 no biliary passage support cholestasis; normal GB/no dilation, no clay stools refute obstruction.
